title: Buying or Importing a Car as a Foreign Resident in Türkiye (MA–MZ Plates)
seoTitle: Buying or Importing a Car in Türkiye: MA–MZ Plates Guide
metaDescription: Compare tax-free MA–MZ blue plates, local Turkish car ÖTV taxes, the 24-month foreign car rule, and mandatory Trafik & Kasko insurance.
quickAnswer: Foreign residents in Türkiye can either buy a standard local-plate car subject to high ÖTV and KDV taxes, buy or temporarily import a tax-free MA–MZ ("guest") plate vehicle through [TURING](https://turing.tr/ytggk-mavi-karne/) with a refundable deposit, or drive a foreign-registered car for up to 730 days under [Ministry of Trade](https://ticaret.gov.tr/gumruk-islemleri/sikca-sorulan-sorular/bireysel/yolcu-beraberi-tasitlar) rules.

body.text: Navigating vehicle ownership is one of the sharpest financial decisions foreign residents face when relocating to Istanbul, Antalya, Bodrum, or İzmir. At [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/)—an independent, client-paid, flat-fee travel, business, and medical travel advisory run by its two founders in Türkiye ("Paid by our clients. Independent of provider commissions.")—we regularly coordinate relocation reconnaissance visits and practical ground logistics. Important boundary: Itinerary of Türkiye coordinates visits, scheduling, and independent introductions only; customs declarations, tax filings, vehicle registrations, and legal representations belong strictly to licensed Turkish attorneys, customs brokers, SMMM accountants, and official authorities.
How do tax-free MA–MZ blue plates work vs buying a regular local-plate car?

MA–MZ plates—often called guest plates (misafir plaka)—allow eligible foreign residents holding a Turkish work permit, student permit, or foreign pension status to buy a tax-free vehicle from another foreigner or import one temporarily without paying ÖTV or KDV. Standard local plates incur full Turkish taxes but can be resold freely to any buyer.

Under [TURING's YTGGK (Blue Carnet) framework](https://turing.tr/ytggk-mavi-karne/) and [Ministry of Foreign Affairs vehicle guidelines](https://www.mfa.gov.tr/araclarla-ilgili-hususlar.tr.mfa), MA–MZ cars require a refundable customs guarantee deposit held by TURING based on the vehicle's engine size and value. When you leave Türkiye or sell the car, you can only transfer an MA–MZ vehicle to another eligible foreigner or export it. By contrast, a regular local-plate car has a liquid resale market among Turkish citizens and residents, requires no TURING deposit, and can be driven by any licensed driver rather than only the permit holder and immediate family.

body.text: Why is Türkiye's ÖTV car tax so high on standard purchases?

Türkiye applies a tiered Special Consumption Tax (Özel Tüketim Vergisi, or ÖTV) under [Law No. 4760](https://gib.gov.tr/mevzuat/kanun/437) based on engine displacement, powertrain type, and pre-tax vehicle value, and then charges 20% VAT (KDV) on top of the combined base price plus ÖTV. This cascading formula frequently doubles or triples showroom prices compared with European or North American markets.

Because ÖTV brackets jump steeply above 1,600 cc and 2,000 cc—and because KDV is calculated on the tax-inclusive subtotal—even mid-range sedans and SUVs carry a substantial fiscal markup. Electric vehicles face separate kilowatt-based brackets, yet higher-powered imports still attract significant duties. For families relocating for two to three years, comparing the depreciation and capital outlay of a local-plate purchase against an MA–MZ purchase or long-term lease is essential before committing capital.
How long can a foreign-registered car stay in Türkiye (24-month rule)?

Under the [Ministry of Trade's Passenger Vehicle FAQ](https://ticaret.gov.tr/gumruk-islemleri/sikca-sorulan-sorular/bireysel/yolcu-beraberi-tasitlar) and [2026 Foreign-Plated Vehicle Passenger Guide](https://ticaret.gov.tr/data/5d4831d913b8762b40ceade8/Rehber-05.01.2026.pdf), a foreign-registered car can stay in Türkiye for up to 730 days (24 months) provided the driver has spent at least 185 days abroad within the 365 days preceding entry, verified automatically via passport entry-exit records.

Once the 730-day allowance is exhausted, both the vehicle and the owner must physically remain outside Türkiye for at least 185 days before bringing a foreign-plated car back under the same exemption. Leaving the car in Türkiye while you fly abroad requires notifying customs in advance and committing that no unauthorized person will drive it—or leaving it under customs supervision. If you are planning seasonal stays, our [Türkiye winter travel guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/turkey-in-winter-premium-travel-guide) covers road conditions and regional driving logistics across colder months.

Every motor vehicle driven on Turkish roads must hold Compulsory Traffic Liability Insurance (Zorunlu Trafik Sigortası), which covers third-party bodily injury and property damage up to statutory limits. Comprehensive coverage (Kasko) is optional by law but strongly recommended to protect your own vehicle against collision, theft, hail, and natural disasters.

You can compare policy tiers and check a used car's accident history (Tramer records) through the [Insurance Information and Monitoring Center (SBM)](https://www.sbm.org.tr/tr/tramer-ile-sorgulama) and its [traffic premium comparison portal](https://www.sbm.org.tr/tr/uygulama/trafik-prim-karsilastirmasi-3). Foreign-plated cars entering Türkiye must carry a valid International Motor Insurance Card (Green Card) covering Türkiye or purchase border traffic insurance at entry.
Pre-Purchase & Import Checklist for Foreign Residents

items: Confirm your residence permit category (work, student, or foreign pension) before pricing MA–MZ plates.
Verify your exact 185-day abroad calculation using official passport entry-exit dates before driving a foreign-plated car across the border.
Run an SBM Tramer damage history check and independent mechanical inspection on any used local or MA–MZ vehicle.
Confirm current TURING guarantee deposit requirements and annual renewal fees with a licensed customs broker.
Secure Compulsory Trafik Insurance immediately upon registration and request Kasko quotes covering Bosphorus-area hail and glass damage.

faq.q: Can a tourist-residence permit holder buy an MA–MZ plate car?
faq.a: Standard short-term tourist residence permit holders generally do not qualify for MA–MZ guest plates. Eligibility is typically tied to active work permits, enrolled university student status, or documented foreign pensioner status, subject to customs verification.

faq.q: Can my Turkish friend borrow my MA–MZ or foreign-plated car?
faq.a: No. Customs regulations strictly restrict who may drive temporarily imported or MA–MZ vehicles. Allowing an unauthorized driver behind the wheel can result in severe customs fines and cancellation of the vehicle's temporary import status.

faq.q: Do foreign-plated cars need Turkish vehicle inspection (TÜVTÜRK)?
faq.a: Foreign-plated cars operating under the 730-day tourist allowance follow their home country's registration validity, whereas MA–MZ and local-plate vehicles registered in Türkiye must pass periodic Turkish TÜVTÜRK safety inspections.

faq.q: How is the TURING deposit refunded when I sell an MA–MZ car?
faq.a: Once the vehicle is formally exported through customs or legally transferred to another eligible foreigner and the Blue Carnet (YTGGK) is closed, TURING processes the refund of the guarantee deposit according to its official procedures.

faq.q: Does buying a local-plate car require a Turkish driving license?
faq.a: You can purchase and register a local-plate car using your Foreigner ID (YKN) and passport, though you must hold a valid driving license—and convert your foreign license after six months of stay—to drive it legally.

faq.q: Can I keep a foreign-plated car in Türkiye while I fly home for a month?
faq.a: Yes, provided you submit a formal customs undertaking confirming the vehicle will remain parked and unused during your absence, or store it in a customs-supervised lot as outlined by the Ministry of Trade.
